decisions.reason: The referral-code source does not change the resale-transfer rules, which are independently established by another clause in the same message.
The same-message INTRODUCE already records that each NFT's mint number is its permanent referral code and identifies its display surfaces.
Using an NFT's mint number as its referral code does not alter the unlimited-mint ebook collection model.
The referral-code attribute source does not change whether secondary royalties are enabled or their flat $10 amount.
The same-message INTRODUCE already captures both the mint-number referral-code identity and its appearance in NFT metadata.
Defining the referral code as the NFT's mint number does not change the commission amount, trigger, recipient, destination, timing, or limit.
The referral-code attribute source does not change badge milestones, award conditions, or on-chain badge recording.
Adding the mint-number referral identity to NFT metadata does not change the separate Small and Big Block ticket counters or their reset behavior.
The source decision concerns the identity of a supplied referral code and does not alter allocation when no referral code is used.
The referral-code identity does not change ticket issuance quantities, recipient, eligibility cycles, or the exclusion of secondary sales.
The referral-code attribute source does not change the mint price or allocation of primary-sale revenue.
The referral-code identity does not change the manual one-click prize claim flow or its Winners page location.
